source.author: verg
source.text: Quid qui, ne gravidis procumbat culmus aristis, luxuriem segetum tenera depascit in herba, cum primum sulcos aequant sata.
source.text_original: Quid qui, ne gravidis procumbat culmus aristis, / luxuriem segetum tenera depascit in herba, / cum primum sulcos aequant sata.
source.text_english: What of the man who, lest the stalk bend down under its heavy ears, grazes the luxuriance of the crops with tender grass, as soon as the seeds level the furrows?

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: quomodo enim laetae segetes et uberes agri interdum culmis aristisque luxuriant, ita praeclara ingenia et mens plena uirtutibus in uariarum artium redundat elegantiam.
reuse.text_original: quomodo enim laetae segetes et uberes agri interdum culmis aristisque luxuriant, ita praeclara ingenia et mens plena uirtutibus in uariarum artium redundat elegantiam.
reuse.text_english: For just as happy harvests and fertile fields sometimes overflow with stalks and ears of grain, so outstanding talents and a mind full of virtues overflow into the elegance of various arts.
